facts.statement: Ornatops is a genus of saurolophine hadrosaur known as the "ornate face" that lived in the Upper Cretaceous of New Mexico.
facts.quote: Ornatops (meaning "ornate face") is a genus of brachylophosaurin saurolophine hadrosaur from the Upper Cretaceous Menefee Formation of New Mexico, United States.

facts.statement: The fossil material of Ornatops was first discovered in 2018 in the Menefee Formation of New Mexico.
facts.quote: Ornatops was originally discovered in 2018 within the Menefee Formation of New Mexico, United States.

facts.statement: The genus was formally described in 2021 based on the relatively complete and articulated holotype specimen WSC 10058.
facts.quote: The specimen was described on the basis of a relatively complete and articulated specimen WSC 10058 in 2021.

facts.statement: The holotype includes a well-preserved skull without jaws, vertebrae, ribs, and limb bones, making it the most complete dinosaur found in the Menefee Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype consists of a well-preserved skull lacking the maxillae and lower jaws, two dorsal vertebrae, a rib, ossified tendons, the right scapula, most of the right humerus, ulna, and radius, the second and third right metacarpals as well as an incomplete ilium and ischium, making it the most complete dinosaur from the Menefee Formation.

facts.statement: The generic name Ornatops means "ornate face" and refers to the elaborate nasofrontal suture on the skull.
facts.quote: Its generic name, Ornatops, means "ornate face" from Latin ornatus and Greek ops, in reference to the elaborate nasofrontal suture.

facts.statement: The species name incantatus means "enchanted" and references New Mexico's nickname, the "Land of Enchantment".
facts.quote: The specific name, incantatus, means "enchanted"; it is a reference to New Mexico's moniker, the "Land of Enchantment".

facts.statement: Ornatops is the first known crested brachylophosaurin found in southern Laramidia, highlighting the diversity of this group in North America during the Campanian.
facts.quote: Because of this, Ornatops is the first crested brachylophosaurin found so far in southern Laramidia, which illustrates how diverse and distributed the clade was in North America during the Campanian.

facts.statement: McDonald et al. classify Ornatops within the subfamily Saurolophinae and the tribe Brachylophosaurini.
facts.quote: McDonald et al. place Ornatops in the Saurolophinae, specifically in the tribe Brachylophosaurini.

facts.statement: Ornatops lived approximately 78 million years ago in what is now New Mexico, United States.
facts.quote: Ornatops incantatus was a genus of brachylophosaurin hadrosaurid that existed in what is now New Mexico, United States approximately 78 million years ago.

facts.statement: Ornatops lived during the late Upper Cretaceous, specifically the Campanian stage, about 78 million years ago in North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico superior, hace aproximadamente 78 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Ornatops is recorded as the Campanian stage, spanning from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: MacDonald and colleagues placed Ornatops in the subfamily Saurolophinae, specifically within the tribe Brachylophosaurini.
facts.quote: MacDonald y col. colocaron a Ornatops en Saurolophinae, específicamente en la tribu Brachylophosaurini.

facts.statement: The exact body proportions of Ornatops remain undescribed because the original description only examined the cranial skeleton.
facts.quote: The exact proportions of Ornatops remain undescribed as the paper naming and describing the genus only examined the cranial skeleton.

rejected.statement: The skull features an expanded nasofrontal suture with unique bumps, suggesting the animal had some form of crest in life.
rejected.quote: The expanded nasofrontal suture of the holotype skull, which bears a pair of bumps as a unique autapomorphy, suggests that Ornatops in life had some form of crest.
